topic: Unveiling Conic Sections: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres
target_audience: High school students interested in geometry or introductory college math students.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Conic Anatomy
lecture_lines: Meet the cone and the slicing plane.
animations: Draw a 3D cone outline in white (#FFFFFF).
Highlight the cone base circle in yellow (#FFFF00).
Label the vertex point with 'V' in blue (#0000FF).

sections.title: Introduction to Dandelin Spheres
lecture_lines: Dandelin spheres hide inside the cone.
They touch the cone and the plane.
animations: Place a small sphere inside the cone in light blue (#ADD8E6).
Place a second, larger sphere inside the cone in light blue (#ADD8E6).
Position a slicing plane tangent to both spheres in red (#FF0000).

sections.title: The Proof Logic (Focus on Ellipse)
lecture_lines: Tangents from point to sphere are equal.
animations: Highlight the resulting ellipse intersection in green (#00FF00).
Draw lines from a point on ellipse to two tangency points.
Highlight distance sum segments in orange (#FFA500).
Mark focal points F1 and F2 in cyan (#00FFFF).
Animate a point traversing the ellipse path smoothly.

sections.title: Visualizing the Family of Curves
lecture_lines: Tilt the plane to change shapes.
The sphere shifts with the tilt.
animations: Rotate the plane angle until it becomes parallel to a generator.
Show the sphere shifting position along the cone axis.
Highlight the resulting parabolic intersection in magenta (#FF00FF).

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
animations: Show a summary table comparing ellipse, parabola, and hyperbola.
Flash the focus-directrix definition text in yellow (#FFFF00).
Display a simple orbital path diagram for visualization.
